gates.gate: Recording state changes without media execution
gates.invariant: A provider that does not register an executable recording contract must return NotSupported and must never publish a recording-started/stopped success event or flip Interaction.RecordingState; a provider that does register the contract must prove a real provider media command was issued and a durable recording session was persisted, not just a state flag. Today `ContactCenterRecordingService.StartAsync`/`StopAsync` flips `RecordingState` and publishes success events with no provider media command (`ContactCenterRecordingService.cs:28-79`) and `IContactCenterVoiceProvider` exposes no recording operation.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterSupportMatrixTests.cs proves `.github/contact-center/support-matrix.v1.json` declares recording prohibited for every GA-Core provider profile (policy-level fail-closed). ContactCenterRecordingAndMonitoringTests.StartAsync_WithoutExecutableProviderContract_StillSetsRecordingStateAndPublishesSuccess explicitly reproduces the unfixed state-without-execution runtime behavior; the runtime NotSupported/durable-session proof remains a planned:contact-center-domain-invariants R4/R8 dependency.

gates.gate: Monitor/whisper/barge/take-over can report success without execution
gates.invariant: A provider that advertises only the Whisper capability must expose and execute only Whisper; Monitor, Barge, and TakeOver must each fail with NotSupported unless that specific operation is separately certified and executed by the provider, never inferred from a single combined capability flag. Today `ContactCenterMonitoringService.EngageAsync` checks `ContactCenterVoiceProviderCapabilities` and publishes `SupervisorMonitorStarted` with no per-operation provider execution proof (`ContactCenterMonitoringService.cs:33-74`).
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterSupportMatrixTests.cs proves `.github/contact-center/support-matrix.v1.json` declares monitor/whisper/barge/take-over prohibited for every GA-Core provider profile (policy-level fail-closed). ContactCenterRecordingAndMonitoringTests.EngageAsync_WithCapabilityFlagButNoExecutableOperation_StillPublishesSuccess explicitly reproduces today's capability-flag-only runtime behavior; a Whisper-only provider test double that must fail Monitor/Barge/TakeOver at runtime is a planned:contact-center-domain-invariants R4/R8 dependency.

gates.gate: Session loss during wrap-up permanently consumes capacity
gates.invariant: If the agent client crashes or disconnects during after-call work, the persisted `WrapUpDeadlineUtc`/required-disposition state must be swept server-side after its grace period so the interaction reaches a deterministic, auditable terminal state and the agent's capacity is released; capacity release must never depend on a connected client. Today after-call work is not persisted with a server-swept deadline, so a crash during wrap-up can leave a nonterminal interaction consuming capacity indefinitely (`ContactCenterHub.cs:113-126`; `AgentSessionStore.cs:35-40`).
gates.evidenceLocation: AgentWorkStateHealingServiceTests.Interaction_AfterCallStateHasNoServerSweptDeadlineToday pins the current missing persisted WrapUpDeadlineUtc contract. AgentSessionServiceTests.DisconnectAsync_WhenLastConnection_DoesNotSignOutAvailableProfileToday proves disconnect does not trigger profile/work-state recovery. R3 must replace these characterizations with a server-swept deadline and deterministic capacity-release proof across all supported databases/topologies.

gates.gate: Completed-handler identity unstable across deployment
gates.invariant: Outbox completed-handler keys are stable, explicit, versioned ids; under a rolling deployment that reorders or renames handler registrations, only handlers that were never recorded as completed under their stable id may replay, and a permanently failing handler is isolated so it never blocks other due work.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterOutboxTests.DispatchDueAsync_AfterHandlerOrderChanges_DoesNotReplayCompletedHandler and DispatchDueAsync_WhenFirstDueMessageFails_ContinuesToLaterMessage prove stable versioned handler checkpoints and per-message poison isolation. Constructor validation tests reject blank, duplicate, and unspecified handler contracts.

gates.gate: Ambiguous inbound matches attributed to first contact
gates.invariant: When inbound contact lookup returns more than one match, the activity must persist a deterministic candidate set and an explicit ambiguous-resolution state instead of auto-assigning the first match. The call may continue through contact-independent routing, but completion must require an authorized explicit candidate selection and no contact-bound subject action may run before resolution.
gates.evidenceLocation: InboundVoiceServiceTests proves zero, one, and unordered duplicate lookup matches persist Unresolved, Resolved, and deterministic Ambiguous states without first-match fallback while ambiguous calls remain routable. OmnichannelActivityTests pins candidate validation, immutable reattribution, audit metadata, and idempotency. DefaultActivityDispositionServiceTests proves the source-neutral completion boundary rejects unresolved ambiguity, and AgentWorkspaceEndpoints requires resource-scoped CompleteActivity authorization. DefaultSubjectActionExecutorTests proves unresolved, ambiguous, and legacy unknown inbound activities cannot mutate contacts or create follow-up work. ContactResolutionUiArchitectureTests proves completion renders the required candidate selector, resolves the activity in the display driver, and reloads the selected contact before disposition.

gates.gate: Calling-window gate insufficient for regulated automated dialing
gates.invariant: Outbound dialing eligibility must evaluate the reused business-hours calendar (day-of-week, holidays, minute precision, time zone), rolling abandonment rate, and safe-harbor behavior before any attempt, and the automatic Power/Progressive/Predictive dialing modes must remain unavailable until every one of those checks is certified by tests and legal/product policy. `DefaultDialerEligibilityService.cs:153-173` evaluates only an hour-only window today and omits day-of-week, holidays, minute precision, regional policy, abandonment caps, and safe-harbor behavior.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/DialerEligibilityServiceTests.cs and BusinessHoursServiceTests.cs cover the current hour-only window and business-hours calendar; calendar/holiday/time-zone precision, rolling abandonment caps, safe-harbor behavior, and the automated-mode gate are a planned:contact-center-domain-invariants dependency.

gates.gate: Raw inbound-event endpoint duplicates ingress and broad privilege
gates.invariant: The authenticated `api/contact-center/voice/inbound` endpoint must never let a manager or agent synthesize a provider call under the broad `ManageInteractions` permission, and the simulator path it supports must be unavailable in a Production-configured host. `VoiceIngressEndpoint.cs` authorizes only `ContactCenterPermissions.ManageInteractions` and duplicates the signed provider webhook ingress with no Production/environment guard.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/InboundVoiceServiceTests.cs covers routing behavior once the endpoint is invoked; a dedicated non-manager-denied and Production-unavailable proof for `VoiceIngressEndpoint` is a planned:contact-center-domain-invariants dependency.

gates.gate: Capability flags exceed executable contracts
gates.invariant: A voice provider must fail registration/selection when it advertises a capability flag for an operation it does not implement; a capability flag and a success-shaped domain event are never proof that provider work occurred. Live media is exposed only by a matching `IContactCenterVoiceMediaProvider` registration under the dependency-only media features, while Recording, Monitor, Whisper, Barge, and TakeOver require both their capability metadata and matching executable contracts.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterVoiceMediaProviderResolverTests proves executable-registration-only media resolution; ContactCenterRecordingAndMonitoringTests and ContactCenterTransferServiceTests prove capability-plus-contract enforcement and provider-confirmed state for recording, monitoring, and transfer.

gates.gate: Disconnected agents remain routable
gates.invariant: After an agent's last live connection disconnects, routing must never offer that agent new work, and no reservation may be created for the agent until a session reconnects; canonical eligibility must join a manager-owned `QueueMembership` with a live `AgentAvailability` projection, not a bare `AgentProfile.Available` flag. Today disconnect marks the `AgentSession` offline, but routing selects `AgentProfile` by Available presence without requiring a live session (`ContactCenterHub.cs:113-126`; `AgentProfileStore.cs:40-45`).
gates.evidenceLocation: AgentSessionServiceTests.DisconnectAsync_WhenLastConnection_DoesNotSignOutAvailableProfileToday proves the last disconnect only marks the session offline, while ActivityAssignmentServiceTests.AssignNextAsync_WhenAvailableProfileHasNoLiveSession_StillReservesToday proves assignment does not consult live-session state. R3 must invert this into a disconnect-then-no-reservation invariant using canonical AgentAvailability across the supported database/topology matrix.

gates.gate: Provider call outlives failed reservation acceptance
gates.invariant: A dialer attempt must never call the provider before its reservation is accepted; if provider execution partially succeeds after a failed acceptance, a compensating hangup command must be issued using an idempotent command id so no active call outlives its failed reservation. `DialerAttemptService.cs:93-118,145-170` can dial before reservation acceptance today with no provider hangup compensation on failure.
gates.evidenceLocation: DialerAttemptServiceTests.TryDialAsync_WhenProviderSucceedsButReservationAcceptanceFails_DropsProviderCallIdentityToday proves a successful provider call can outlive failed reservation acceptance while its provider call id is discarded, and TryDialAsync_WhenProviderTimesOutAfterUnknownExecution_MarksDefinitiveFailureToday proves an unknown provider outcome is treated as a definitive failure and the work is removed. R3 must invert these characterizations with accept-and-command persistence before execution, durable OutcomeUnknown reconciliation, and idempotent compensation.

gates.gate: Provider event dedupe check-then-insert
gates.invariant: Under two concurrent service instances racing the same shared database with a duplicated or out-of-order provider event, canonical provider identity, a unique `(CanonicalProviderKey, ProviderCallId)` constraint on CallSession, and a unique provider-event-id constraint on the inbox must together guarantee exactly one valid state transition. `ProviderVoiceEventService.cs:125-147,221-257` deduplicates with a check-then-insert read today, and `CallSessionIndexMigrations.cs:32-47` does not enforce a unique provider-call identity.
gates.evidenceLocation: DefaultContactCenterEventPublisherTests.PublishAsync_WhenConcurrentDuplicatesBothReadMissing_PersistsBothToday proves concurrent duplicate idempotency checks can both persist and enqueue the same logical event. ProviderVoiceEventServiceTests.IngestAsync_WhenOutOfOrderEventHasEqualTimestamp_RegressesConnectedCallToday proves timestamp-only ordering can regress Connected to Ringing, while IngestAsync_WhenProviderNameChanged_FallsBackByCallIdAndCanonicalizesStoredProvider proves raw provider names are mutated rather than resolved through stable canonical identity. R3 must invert these characterizations with provider inbox uniqueness, provider sequence/high-water rules, and canonical provider keys across the supported database matrix.

gates.gate: Distributed locks lack DB CAS
gates.invariant: Under two application nodes racing a distributed-lock expiry on the same queue item or reservation, database row versions/conditional writes and unique active queue-item/reservation constraints must guarantee exactly one accepted reservation; the lock is a contention optimization, never the correctness authority.
gates.evidenceLocation: ActivityReservationSharedDatabaseTests.ReserveAsync_TwoProvidersReadWaitingState_OnlyOnePersistsReservation runs two independent service providers and YesSql sessions against one SQLite database, synchronizes both reads before either commit, deliberately permits overlapping activity and agent lock holders, and proves document-version CAS leaves exactly one pending reservation while the loser receives a database concurrency failure. The same suite verifies unique active activity, pending-agent, and queue-item claims while terminal history remains insertable; ActivityReservationServiceTests.ReserveAsync_WhenConcurrentTransitionWins_ThrowsAndAbortsScope proves the canceled YesSql session is not reset or reused; ContactCenterClaimMigrationTests proves valid legacy backfill and actionable failure on duplicate legacy claims. The planned contact-center-database-matrix must repeat this invariant on every supported production database before certification.

gates.gate: Hot-query indexes mismatch predicates
gates.invariant: Every hot queue, outbox, and active-call query must be led by an index that covers its actual filter columns, and the resulting query plan must be verified with an explicit query-count/plan test on every supported database. Hot queue, outbox, and active-call queries are not currently led by their filter columns.
gates.evidenceLocation: No query-count/plan contract test exists yet; per-database covering-index verification is a planned:contact-center-database-matrix dependency.

gates.gate: Routing/live metrics scale linearly
gates.invariant: Routing candidate selection and live metrics must use bounded top-N queries and aggregate SQL rather than broad loads with per-agent active-count queries, and must meet the approved SLO at every supported capacity tier: 100, 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000 agents/interactions. Routing today loads broad sets and performs per-agent active-count queries instead of bounded top-N aggregation.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/CapacityRoutingStrategyTests.cs and QueueItemPrioritizerTests.cs cover routing selection logic at unit scale; the 100/1k/10k/100k SLO load proof is a planned:contact-center-database-matrix dependency.

gates.gate: Metrics projections not idempotent/rebuildable
gates.invariant: Every projection increment is guarded by a unique `(Projection, EventId)` processed-event record committed atomically with the effect, while metric rows use optimistic concurrency and portable date/event uniqueness. Every replayable projection must also support a versioned checkpoint, a documented rebuild operation, and a drift-detection check; that rebuild tooling remains incomplete.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterEventDeduplicationPersistenceTests uses real SQLite sessions to prove a failed handler unit leaves neither marker nor metric durable, a retry commits one effect, and concurrent reservations allow only one commit. ContactCenterMetricsServiceTests and ContactCenterWorkflowEventHandlerTests cover handler-level replay branching; outbox tests cover poison isolation. Multi-database certification plus versioned checkpoint, rebuild, and drift-detection proof remain planned:contact-center-database-matrix dependencies.

gates.gate: Callback promotion duplicate-prone/unbounded
gates.invariant: Under two background workers crashing and restarting concurrently, callback promotion must claim a bounded batch with owner/lease expiry so exactly one activity/callback results, never a duplicate promotion or an unbounded scan. Callback promotion is unbounded and duplicate-prone today with no lease-based claim.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/CallbackServiceTests.cs characterizes today's promotion logic at unit scale; the two-worker crash/restart exactly-once proof is a planned:contact-center-operations-gates dependency.

gates.gate: Provider reconciliation unbounded/overlaps
gates.invariant: Under a chaos scenario with a slow provider and overlapping worker executions across 100,000 calls, provider reconciliation must checkpoint its scan and rate-limit external lookups so overlapping runs never duplicate work or fall behind unboundedly. Provider reconciliation is unbounded today with no checkpointed, overlap-safe scan.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ProviderCallStateSynchronizationServiceTests.cs and ProviderVoiceOfferSynchronizationServiceTests.cs characterize today's reconciliation logic at unit scale; the slow-provider chaos/overlapping-worker proof at 100,000 calls is a planned:contact-center-operations-gates dependency.

gates.gate: Telephony interaction writes were last-write-wins
gates.invariant: Every write to a telephony interaction is guarded by an optimistic-concurrency check, so a writer that mutated a version another writer has already replaced fails instead of silently discarding the winner's work. Every read-modify-write path re-reads the interaction inside a dedicated session and reapplies its mutation against the committed version, which means a concurrent writer's field survives the retry and a state guard evaluated before the retry is re-evaluated against the version that actually won.
gates.evidenceLocation: TelephonyInteractionStoreConcurrencyTests, which exercises DefaultTelephonyInteractionStore against a real SQLite database, plus the retrying-update assertions in AsteriskRealtimeVoiceEventDispatcherTests, DefaultIncomingCallDispatcherTests, and TelephonyInteractionSynchronizationServiceTests.

gates.gate: Base coupled to Omnichannel Managements UI
gates.invariant: The base `CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter` feature must boot and activate in a tenant alone, resolving every service from only its own declared manifest dependencies, without requiring `CrestApps.OrchardCore.Omnichannel.Managements` or any other administration-integration assembly. The base feature now declares `CrestApps.OrchardCore.Omnichannel.Activities`, the headless half of the Omnichannel management module, and the administration experience is reachable only through a feature a deployment opts into.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterFeatureDependencyArchitectureTests.cs and the ledger .github/contact-center/feature-dependency-violations.v1.json statically prove and pin every declared manifest dependency and the full transitive closure of every Contact Center feature, and fail the build if any new undeclared coupling appears; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter.FeatureActivationTests/ContactCenterHeadlessClosureTests.cs supplies the runtime proof by booting a fresh tenant with the whole headless closure and resolving every navigation provider and display driver the tenant can produce.

gates.gate: Queues/Voice/RealTime/SoftPhone dependencies inconsistent
gates.invariant: Every service registered by a feature's Startup class must resolve using only that feature's declared transitive manifest dependencies. A singleton and supported-combination activation matrix must prove that enabling Queues, Voice, RealTime, and SoftPhone in every approved combination never fails to resolve a service. Today `QueuesStartup` registers a Telephony soft-phone driver requiring `HubRouteManager` without declaring Telephony or SignalR/RealTime, and Voice depends on `Telephony.SoftPhone` (`ContactCenter/Startup.cs:210-262,337-420`; `ContactCenterSoftPhoneWidgetDisplayDriver.cs:24-80`).
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterFeatureDependencyArchitectureTests.cs statically parses every Contact Center StartupBase class across the module, resolves each recognized registered concrete type's constructor parameters, and fails the build if a parameter resolves to a service not guaranteed by the registering feature's manifest closure or its RequireFeatures closure. The ledger .github/contact-center/feature-dependency-violations.v1.json pins the two currently known findings: Voice's declared coupling to Telephony.SoftPhone (FDV002) and Queues' undeclared runtime requirement on SignalR's HubRouteManager through ContactCenterSoftPhoneWidgetDisplayDriver (FDV003). Factory/non-generic registrations and runtime singleton/combination activation across every approved Queues/Voice/RealTime/SoftPhone combination remain planned:contact-center-feature-activation-matrix dependencies.

gates.gate: Workflow bridge not independently feature-gated
gates.invariant: A tenant must be able to enable or disable a real `CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter.Workflows` feature independently of the base Contact Center features. Today the Workflows bridge activates only implicitly through `[RequireFeatures("OrchardCore.Workflows")]` with no independently selectable Contact Center feature.
gates.evidenceLocation: No independent Workflows-bridge feature or enable/disable test exists yet; this is a planned:contact-center-feature-activation-matrix dependency.

gates.gate: Provider modules depend on implementation/Asterisk integrations ungated
gates.invariant: Asterisk and DialPad provider assemblies must reference only `CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter.Abstractions` (or another stable abstraction package), never a Contact Center implementation assembly, and each provider's base/adapter features must boot independently. Provider modules currently reference Contact Center implementation assemblies, and Asterisk registers Contact Center adapters from its base feature.
gates.evidenceLocation: No assembly-reference architecture test or independent provider-base/adapter boot test exists yet; this is a planned:contact-center-feature-activation-matrix dependency.

gates.gate: Omnichannel Managements dynamically resolves optional CC services
gates.invariant: `CrestApps.OrchardCore.Omnichannel.Managements` must run standalone with Contact Center features disabled and must resolve optional Contact Center contributors (for example dialer services) only through an Omnichannel-owned contributor contract, never through reverse references or ad hoc service location that assumes Contact Center is present. Omnichannel Managements currently resolves optional dialer services dynamically via service location.
gates.evidenceLocation: No Managements-only activation test with Contact Center contributors present/absent exists yet; this is a planned:contact-center-feature-activation-matrix dependency.

gates.gate: Post-commit uses IServiceProvider/ad hoc child scopes
gates.invariant: Post-commit handler and hub execution must become an explicit, testable dispatcher abstraction; before that refactor lands, the current `IServiceProvider`/ad hoc shell-child-scope execution path must be characterized by tests so the refactor cannot silently change behavior. Concrete orchestration types and post-commit/hub execution currently hide dependencies behind service location and child scopes.
gates.evidenceLocation: No characterization test for the current post-commit/child-scope execution path exists yet; it must land before the explicit-dispatcher refactor as a planned:contact-center-feature-activation-matrix dependency.

gates.gate: Feature disable has no quiesce or re-enable contract
gates.invariant: Every feature-owned Contact Center task, hub, listener, adapter, and media provider must declare how it stops accepting work, drains admitted work, and reconciles in a fresh scope after shell activation. Orchard pre-disable callbacks must quiesce matching participants before descriptor mutation, activation must not perform provider or database work inline, and inactive or idle disable/re-enable must not retain tenant-local runtime state.
gates.evidenceLocation: `.github/contact-center/feature-lifecycle-contracts.v1.json` defines inactive, idle, and R3 active-work contracts. `ContactCenterFeatureLifecycleTests` proves admission rejection, quiesce-before-drain ordering, bounded timeout signaling, admission remaining closed during teardown, connected-hub abortion, fresh-scope Voice reconciliation, and complete background-task ledger coverage. Provider, endpoint, dialer, command, outbox, and media tests prove new work is rejected after quiesce, admitted work retains a drain lease, provider-feature rejection before provider contact returns a command to delayed Pending, media cleanup retains its lease until success, unavailable expected outbox handlers cannot silently disappear or consume the dead-letter budget, and durable command/inbox/outbox state resumes through existing ownership and fencing. Fresh-tenant activation proves every GA-Core profile resolves the lifecycle manager and participants through its declared dependency closure. Multi-node process-crash and rolling-deployment certification remains an R8 topology gate.

gates.gate: Headless deployment carries no administration surface
gates.invariant: A deployment that serves no user interface must be able to enable every Contact Center capability without activating one. Screens are not part of a capability: each capability feature registers only services, and the screens it used to register live in a separate administration feature that depends on the capability rather than the other way round, so enabling the capability can never pull the user interface in. This holds across the module boundary as well - the Omnichannel management module is split into a headless activity feature the Contact Center base depends on and the administration experience, and the Telephony provider settings screen is likewise separated from the telephony services - because a capability that transitively drags an administration module in is no more headless than one that registers the screens itself. Routes count as surface as much as services do, because moving a screen's driver without its controller leaves the route registered and authorized while the display pipeline that binds and validates its form no longer resolves, so the write path silently persists whatever the empty editor produced. The proof is structural rather than a list of feature names: the whole headless closure is booted in a tenant and every navigation provider, display driver, and routed administration controller the tenant can resolve is enumerated, so a screen added to a capability feature later fails without anyone remembering to extend the test. The features excluded from that closure are the ones that exist to serve a user interface, and each is required to prove it serves one, so the closure cannot be weakened by moving a headless feature onto the exclusion list. A feature is required to contribute surface of its own rather than inherit it - its declared dependency closure is booted with the feature withheld and that surface subtracted - because every administration feature depends on the administration root and would otherwise satisfy the requirement on the root's screens alone. Every administration feature must in turn register screens of its own beyond those it inherits, because an administration feature that registers nothing is a support liability that silently does nothing when enabled.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter.FeatureActivationTests/ContactCenterHeadlessClosureTests.cs boots one tenant with every Contact Center feature that is not a user experience and asserts that no excluded feature was activated and that the tenant resolves no navigation provider, display driver, or routed [Admin] controller from the Contact Center, Telephony, or Omnichannel assemblies, the controllers being read from the tenant's own IActionDescriptorCollectionProvider so the sweep reflects what the tenant routes rather than what the assembly compiles; EveryUserExperienceFeature_ActuallyServesAUserInterface boots each excluded feature alone and requires it to register Contact Center or Telephony surface of its own, so the exclusion list cannot be padded to weaken the closure; EveryAdministrationFeature_RegistersTheSurfaceItsCapabilityGaveUp boots each administration feature alone and requires screens beyond those inherited from the administration root, which is what proves the root and the five capability administration features are not empty markers; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterFeatureDependencyArchitectureTests.cs pins the resulting manifest graph and the transitive closure of every feature in .github/contact-center/feature-dependency-violations.v1.json.

gates.gate: No production health/OpenTelemetry
gates.invariant: Contact Center must publish an `ActivitySource` with structured correlation, a `Meter` with counters/histograms for routing/queue/reservation/outbox/provider-command outcomes, and a health endpoint reporting degraded/unhealthy state for database, outbox/dead-letter, background-task lag, provider connectivity, listener lease, and SignalR backplane connectivity. No Contact Center `ActivitySource`, `Meter`, liveness, or readiness model exists today; `DialerActivitySourceHelper` only classifies business activity sources, not distributed traces.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterHealthEndpointsTests, ContactCenterNodeHealthCheckTests, ContactCenterNodeServingHealthCheckTests, ContactCenterTopologyHealthCheckTests, ContactCenterOutboxHealthCheckTests, ContactCenterProcessHealthMiddlewareTests, ContactCenterProcessLivenessPathValidatorTests, NodeServingStateTrackerTests, and SharedHealthCheckEndpointGuardTests prove the liveness/readiness/dependency probe split, the tag-to-predicate binding, node-local readiness, the declared-topology readiness verdict, and the outbox and provider-ingress dependency thresholds. The Meter and its outbox counters are published and asserted. The trace half of this gate is not met: the ActivitySource is declared but no Contact Center span is ever started, so R7 is re-opened by Plan 3 and this gate stays partial until distributed tracing exists.

gates.gate: Multi-node SignalR not configured/proven
gates.invariant: Under two application nodes, a hub offer, a supervisor dashboard watch, an agent reconnect, and a supervisor fan-out broadcast must all reach the correct connections through the supported `CrestApps.OrchardCore.SignalR.Redis` backplane; in-memory single-node behavior must not be used to claim multi-node correctness.
gates.evidenceLocation: SignalRRedisBackplaneArchitectureTests proves the explicit Orchard Redis-dependent feature, invalid-configuration guard, and distinct deployment/shell channel prefixes. TwoNodeRedisBackplaneTests.ProviderEvent_CrossesNodesWithoutCrossingTenantShells boots independent Node A/Node B tenant-scoped transport hosts through the production registration, sends a provider-listener event across nodes, and rejects delivery to an equal user id in another shell. This does not activate a complete Orchard tenant or certify ContactCenterHub; R8 must extend the fixture to authenticated offer, supervisor, reconnect, and fan-out scenarios with retained release evidence.

gates.gate: Logs contain raw customer/agent IDs
gates.invariant: No log entry emitted by a Contact Center or Telephony/SMS provider path may contain an E.164 customer address, another stable personal identifier, a token, or a secret; centralized structured PII classification/redaction must be enforced with negative log tests across every path, not only the Asterisk event-subscription URI. Telephony/SMS logs can currently include raw addresses outside the Asterisk URI case covered by S003.
gates.evidenceLocation: AsteriskSettingsUtilitiesTests and AsteriskWebSecurityTests prove ARI credentials are removed from logged URIs. ContactCenterOperationalLogPrivacyTests now proves the R1 fix: the shared OperationalLogFieldKind/OperationalLogIdentifierCategory/OperationalLogRedactor classification API in CrestApps.OrchardCore.Abstractions pseudonymizes stable identifiers with a process-local random-key HMAC-SHA-256 and fully redacts customer addresses, secrets/token-shaped values, complete metadata dictionaries, free-form request/provider-response text, and exception messages/inner-exception data while retaining exception type and a bounded, control-sanitized stack-frame summary, migrated across all operational logging paths in the Telephony, Asterisk, DialPad, Omnichannel SMS, and Contact Center Core/module surfaces; OperationalLogRedactorTests and the inverted ContactCenterOperationalLogPrivacyTests negative/executed tests prove sentinel E.164 addresses, user/agent/call ids, secrets, raw exceptions, and attacker-controlled stack-trace text never appear while SanitizeLogValue continues to strip CR/LF for log-forging protection. The former hand-pinned source-string assertions were replaced by a Roslyn guard that parses every logging call in the Contact Center, Telephony, Asterisk, DialPad, and Omnichannel SMS trees and fails when any sensitive identifier reaches a logger without passing through OperationalLogRedactor, so the rule now applies to code written after the audit rather than to ten hand-picked files. The dedicated contact-center-operations-gates CI workflow remains planned:contact-center-operations-gates.

gates.gate: Asterisk sample host unsafe
gates.invariant: The Asterisk dashboard development host must reject startup in a Production-configured process, and any request reaching its diagnostics, origination, hangup, or bridge-deletion endpoints anonymously must be unavailable or return 401/403, not succeed. `AsteriskWebSecurity.EnsureDevelopmentOnly` already throws in Production (`CrestApps.OrchardCore.Asterisk.Web/Program.cs:9`), but the dashboard, channel-disconnect, bridge-disconnect, and simulation endpoints in that Program.cs enforce no per-request authorization, so 401/403 defense-in-depth is still missing if the process guard is ever bypassed.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Telephony/AsteriskWebSecurityTests.cs proves the Production startup guard throws and does not throw in Development. The pr_ci.yml job executes the test but does not yet upload a durable result artifact; retained CI output and per-endpoint 401/403 defense-in-depth remain a planned: .github/contact-center/evidence/O004/ dependency.

gates.gate: CI omits browser/provider/feature/performance
gates.invariant: Each regression class (browser/E2E, provider contract, feature-activation, and performance) must run in its own owning CI workflow and fail with retained diagnostic artifacts when that class regresses; a single generic build-and-unit-test job must not be relied on to catch them. `pr_ci.yml` currently defines only one `build_test` job that runs `dotnet build` and `dotnet test`, with no browser install step, provider-contract job, feature-activation job, or performance/chaos job.
gates.evidenceLocation: `.github/workflows/contact_center_feature_activation_matrix.yml` runs the feature-activation class, `.github/workflows/contact_center_browser_gates.yml` runs the browser/E2E class, and `.github/workflows/contact_center_operations_gates.yml` runs the distributed class - each in its own workflow with retained per-run trx artifacts uploaded using `if-no-files-found: error`. The provider-contract and performance/chaos classes still have no owning workflow, so this gate stays partial.

gates.gate: Retention/erasure/rolling-upgrade incomplete
gates.invariant: Every entity carrying customer data (call sessions, Telephony history, metrics, recordings) must define a retention horizon and an erasure transformation, proven by purge and erasure tests, and every destructive schema migration must be proven safe for a mixed-version rolling upgrade using expand-migrate-contract, or the release must explicitly document a required downtime window. Retention today covers only interaction events; call sessions, Telephony history, metrics, recordings, and PII erasure remain undefined, and destructive migrations are unproven for rolling deployment.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterRetentionServiceTests.cs proves purge behavior for interaction events only; per-entity classification/erasure for call sessions, Telephony history, metrics, recordings, and the mixed-version rolling-upgrade migration proof are a planned:contact-center-operations-gates dependency.

gates.gate: Options validated on start; invalid configuration refuses the tenant
gates.invariant: Every operator-supplied options class in the Contact Center, Telephony and provider assemblies is registered with a validator, and an invalid value refuses tenant activation rather than surfacing later through whichever code path reads the option first. Distributed-lock waits, lease expiries, reclamation thresholds and provider HTTP budgets are configuration rather than compiled constants, and each lease expiry must exceed its acquisition timeout.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterOptionsValidationTests enumerates every *Options type in the governed assemblies by reflection and fails when one accepts operator input without a registered IValidateOptions, with discovery pinned by a floor so it cannot pass vacuously and exemptions asserted to name real types; it also pins that ValidateOnStart is inert inside a per-tenant container, which is why TenantOptionsStartupValidator exists. ContactCenterConfigurationFailClosedTests boots a real Orchard host and proves a tenant carrying a negative retention window, a sub-one health threshold or an unrecognized topology profile refuses to activate, with a valid-configuration control proving activation is otherwise reachable.

gates.gate: Preview data export, quiesce, reset and verify
gates.invariant: A tenant that piloted the preview can export every Contact Center document, quiesce all enabled features, delete either operational data or all data, and verify the result. The destructive step is coupled to the recoverable one: reset requires an export receipt derived from live per-data-set counts, so it refuses when the export is stale or the tenant is still admitting work, and it refuses by default, outside development, and on a confirmation token that does not match the tenant. Every persisted document type is classified in one registry, so a new entity cannot escape both export and reset.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterPreviewMaintenanceCompletenessTests compares the data-set registry against the persisted document types discovered by reflection, with a discovery floor so it cannot pass vacuously, and fails when a type is unclassified, duplicated, or mapped to a governance category that does not resolve. ContactCenterPreviewMaintenanceTests exercises export, quiesce, reset and verify against a real YesSql SQLite store and pins each refusal path, that an operational reset preserves operator-authored configuration while an All reset does not, and that a write after the export makes the receipt stale. ContactCenterPreviewMaintenanceActivationTests repeats the whole cycle inside a real Orchard tenant so the container registration, options binding and lifecycle participants are proven, not assumed.

gates.invariant: A node still running the previous schema version keeps reading and writing every Contact Center index table after a node running the current version has upgraded the database, and the upgrade path converges on exactly the schema a fresh installation produces, including the unique constraints. An upgrade step may not add a non-nullable column without a default, drop or narrow a column the previous version still projects, or leave a freshly installed deployment and an upgraded deployment on different shapes.
gates.gate: N-1 rolling upgrade and install-path convergence
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterRollingUpgradeTests builds two real SQLite databases from the shipped migrations. One takes the fresh-installation path, the other is installed at the previous schema version and then upgraded, after which a previous-version writer and a current-version writer both insert into the upgraded tables and the previous version's projection is read back. A third assertion compares every column definition and every unique constraint between the two databases, and discovery floors plus a strict-subset assertion stop the suite passing vacuously. The static additive-migration gate cannot cover this, because adding a non-nullable column with no default is additive and still breaks every previous-version write.

gates.gate: Global supervisor SignalR group
gates.invariant: Given two tenant shells sharing one SignalR hub lifetime manager or production backplane, a supervisor broadcast or user-targeted message scoped to tenant A must never be delivered to any connection belonging to tenant B. `ContactCenterHub` now qualifies the supervisors group and user identifiers with the shell's tenant name through `TenantSignalRGroupName` (`Hubs/ContactCenterHub.cs:32,47,108,121,502-504`).
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/ContactCenterRealTimeNotifierTests.cs proves two concurrently active in-process shells use distinct tenant-qualified user/supervisor destinations. ContactCenterHubSecurityTests.cs constructs the real ContactCenterHub and invokes OnConnectedAsync, proving each permission is evaluated before the corresponding group join, that a connection holding neither Contact Center permission aborts without joining any group, and that every joined destination is tenant-qualified; runtime authorization-denial coverage remains under S002. The pr_ci.yml job executes the tests but does not yet upload a durable result artifact; retained production-backplane evidence remains planned: .github/contact-center/evidence/S001/.

gates.gate: Agents self-enroll arbitrary queues/campaigns
gates.invariant: A hub membership, subscription, or routing-candidacy request for a queue or campaign id must be rejected unless the requesting agent has a manager-owned `QueueMembership`/`CampaignMembership` entitlement for that id; an agent entitled only to queue A must never gain access to queue B.

gates.gate: Production refuses checked-in development credentials
gates.invariant: A tenant running outside development refuses to activate while the Asterisk provider configuration still carries a credential published in this repository, including the Coturn static authentication secret and the Asterisk ARI password, or an unreplaced placeholder. The same values continue to work in development. Where a published secret only derives a client-visible artifact, the guard degrades to STUN-only ICE rather than issuing a forgeable relay credential.

gates.gate: No Orchard tenant feature matrix
gates.invariant: Every Contact Center feature must, on a fresh Orchard tenant, enable, run its migrations, resolve every registered service, participate in routing, and disable cleanly, for every legal manifest combination; no feature may compile while failing as soon as a tenant enables it.

gates.gate: No repeatable multi-node/load/chaos gate
gates.invariant: A repeatable, automated gate must exercise application-node failure, database/Redis dependency failure, reservation/queue contention, and SignalR fan-out under load, and must publish retained pass/fail evidence; no multi-node, network-partition, provider-outage, Redis-outage, rolling-upgrade, or scale claim is approved without it. gates.gate: Asterisk listeners split-brain/stale ordering
gates.invariant: Under two application nodes each subscribed to the same Asterisk tenant event stream, a duplicated or out-of-order provider event must never regress call state; canonical idempotency and a provider sequence/high-water mark must produce exactly one monotonic call state regardless of delivery order or node duplication. Every node can subscribe to the same Asterisk tenant event stream today with no single-writer/monotonic sequence guard (`AsteriskRealtimeVoiceListener.cs:139-149`; `AsteriskRealtimeVoiceEventDispatcher.cs`).

Scenarios duplicate-provider-stream-two-process and listener-lease-loss in .github/contact-center/r0b-harness-dependency-ledger.v1.json define the missing two-process prerequisites and evidence targets; execution remains planned:contact-center-provider-contract-suite.

gates.gate: Client disconnect cancels PBX commands
gates.invariant: A state-changing PBX/provider command must use a server-owned idempotent command id and complete to a terminal state independent of the requesting client; aborting the requesting client's SignalR socket while the command is in flight must never cancel it. `ContactCenterHub` methods thread `Context.ConnectionAborted` through session/state-changing calls (`Hubs/ContactCenterHub.cs:88,167,257,288,331,372`), so a client disconnect can cancel a command mid-flight today.
gates.evidenceLocation: No test currently aborts the client socket mid-command and asserts the server-side command still reaches a terminal state; this is a planned:contact-center-provider-contract-suite dependency.

gates.gate: Webhook buffering/request abort coupling
gates.invariant: Every provider webhook route must enforce provider-specific body-size and authenticated rate limits, a tenant-local concurrency ceiling, and a bounded provider-signed freshness window, then accept the event into a durable inbox before returning success independent of the inbound HTTP request. The body-size ceiling must be enforced against the bytes that actually arrive rather than against the length the caller declares, because a caller that wants to send more than it is allowed to omits the header, and the body must be refused as it arrives rather than after it has been buffered and decoded. The tenant-local concurrency ceiling must be taken before the body is buffered, because that permit is what bounds how many bodies the process holds in memory at once. Oversize, over-limit, missing-timestamp, malformed-timestamp, stale, or excessively future payloads must be rejected, unauthenticated traffic must not consume a provider's authenticated budget, and a client aborting after durable acceptance must never roll back that acceptance.
gates.evidenceLocation: ProviderWebhookIngressLimiterTests, ProviderVoiceWebhookEndpointTests, ProviderVoiceWebhookProcessorTests, DialPadWebhookEndpointTests, ProviderWebhookInboxTests, ProviderWebhookInboxPersistenceTests, ProviderVoiceEventInboxHandlerTests, DialPadWebhookInboxHandlerTests, and RequestBodyReaderTests prove 1 MiB rejection for a declared length and for a chunked body that declares none, that a body larger than the allowance is refused without being buffered or turned into a string, that a request refused for concurrency is refused without reading a single byte of its body, that a body spanning several buffers is returned whole, that a body the server itself refuses is reported the same way as one the reader refuses, that a body fed under back pressure is still read to completion, tenant-local pre-buffering concurrency rejection, authenticated per-provider rate isolation, HTTP 429/Retry-After behavior, bounded provider-signed delivery age/future skew with missing/malformed/non-UTC rejection, explicit YesSql commit before acceptance returns, provider-delivery duplicate detection under a distributed lock, cancellation-independent persisted dispatch, retry/backoff, poison-message isolation, and dead-lettering. A real client disconnect after durable acceptance, every supported database, every GA provider, and process-crash/restart execution remain planned:contact-center-provider-contract-suite dependencies.

gates.gate: RTP secure boundary/jitter/reorder missing
gates.invariant: No GA-Core profile may enable, advertise, resolve, or expose bidirectional media until Asterisk RTP has a documented secure deployment boundary and certified loss, reordering, jitter, capacity, failover, and node-affinity behavior. The media features remain dependency-only and absent from every approved profile; full transport certification is deferred to R9.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterSupportMatrixTests, ContactCenterFeatureDependencyArchitectureTests, and the fresh-tenant activation matrix prove both GA-Core profiles prohibit and do not register media, while AsteriskRtpPacketCodecTests and AsteriskContactCenterVoiceMediaSessionTests remain development-foundation evidence only. Secure boundary, loss/reorder/jitter, capacity, failover, and node-affinity certification are planned:R9-contact-center-media-certification dependencies.

gates.gate: No provider protocol contract test
gates.invariant: Every Asterisk REST Interface event the realtime voice mapper interprets, every property it depends on, and every REST operation and query parameter the ARI client issues must be declared by the Asterisk REST Interface declarations the Asterisk project publishes for the exact release the single-node container image is pinned to, and those declarations must be vendored verbatim under a hash-verified provenance manifest. Compatibility fallbacks the mapper only tolerates must stay absent from those declarations. DialPad has no vendorable schema, so its webhook contract is payload-bound instead: every provider token the normalizer interprets carries a recorded expectation, and every recorded delivery replays through the signed ingress, the production deserializer, and the production normalizer.
gates.evidenceLocation: AsteriskAriContractProvenanceTests, AsteriskAriEventContractTests, AsteriskAriRestContractTests, and DialPadWebhookContractTests replay the vendored Asterisk declarations and the recorded DialPad deliveries through the production mapper, ARI client, and webhook normalizer. The cassette set lives at tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Telephony/Cassettes.

gates.gate: No call state machine property test
gates.invariant: The provider call state machine must converge to the same terminal session state, interaction status, and domain event set no matter how the provider delivers its lifecycle. Deliveries are generated with duplicates, full replays, arbitrary reordering, clock skew across provider nodes, partially sequenced streams, late backward state regressions, and competing terminal reports, and the resulting session must never regress its lifecycle rank, never resurrect a terminated call, never strand a call that the provider reported terminated, never publish a lifecycle domain event twice, and never leave live-only flags set on a terminated call.
gates.evidenceLocation: CallStateMachinePropertyTests drives the production ProviderVoiceEventService and DefaultContactCenterEventPublisher over 400 seeded adversarial delivery sequences per property. The generator and harness live at tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/StateMachine.

gates.gate: Two call-state vocabularies and no hangup causes
gates.invariant: Translation between the twelve-state Contact Center call vocabulary and the seven-state soft-phone vocabulary may be written in exactly one place, enforced by a source scan of every production file. Every Q.850 release cause an Asterisk release can report must normalize to a provider-neutral hangup cause, and the causes reachable across the Q.850 range must cover the whole provider-neutral vocabulary except the answer-detection outcome, which is proven separately. No call session may reach a terminal state without a recorded hangup cause, proven over the adversarial delivery sequences of the call state machine property suite.
gates.evidenceLocation: AsteriskHangupCauseMapperTests, ContactCenterCallStateProjectionTests, ContactCenterCallStateProjectionArchitectureTests, and the Ingest_WheneverTheSessionEnds_AlwaysRecordsAHangupCause property in CallStateMachinePropertyTests.

gates.gate: One fat provider interface forces every provider to fake every operation
gates.invariant: A telephony provider declares only identity and its advertised capabilities; every call operation lives on a separate capability contract, proven by a provider that compiles and dials while implementing call control alone. An operation executes only when the provider both advertises the capability and implements its declared contract, so advertising without implementing and implementing without advertising both fail closed rather than dispatching. Attended transfer is a distinct capability from blind transfer and is never satisfied by the blind-transfer contract. Every capability flag declares a required contract, and each shipped provider implements the contracts for the widest capability set its own capability source can ever advertise.
gates.evidenceLocation: TelephonyProviderCapabilityContractTests, plus the capability-gating theories in DefaultTelephonyServiceTests.

gates.gate: One vendor's implementation vocabulary is published as the shared platform contract
gates.invariant: Provider-neutral telephony and Contact Center contracts declare no vendor product name and no single-provider call-topology vocabulary, so no future provider inherits a metadata key it can never populate. Result metadata that only one provider writes and no neutral consumer reads is declared inside that provider's own module, is referenced nowhere else in the product, and is proven to still be in real use there. The neutral scan covers the whole neutral surface rather than a token subset, and the forbidden vocabulary is proven to match terms a real provider module genuinely writes.
gates.evidenceLocation: ProviderNeutralContractArchitectureTests, plus the MergeRequest.GetCallIds cases in TelephonyHubAuthorizationTests.

gates.gate: Two consumers of one provider call stream race to claim it, so enabling one silently blinds the other
gates.invariant: One provider delivery is ingested once and observed by every projection. The telephony call-history projection and the Contact Center projection are peers on a provider-neutral normalized stream, not alternatives on a first-wins chain, so enabling Contact Center cannot stop telephony call history from recording an outcome. Ingestion takes exactly one lease per delivery no matter how many projections consume it, including when a projection re-enters ingestion from a fresh scope, and exactly one durable de-duplication record is written per delivery. Only internal call-control orchestration may absorb an event before it reaches the normalized stream.
gates.evidenceLocation: VoiceEventFanOutIntegrationTests, plus the normalized-stream ownership case in ContactCenterFeatureDependencyArchitectureTests.

gates.gate: Routing and the CRM wrote the same activity document, so one of the two writes was lost
gates.invariant: Routing state — assignment status, reservation, assignee, and attempt count — is owned by a Contact Center work state document, and no Contact Center source writes those fields onto the CRM activity except the single projector that reconciles the read model. A reservation commits without touching the CRM activity, so a person editing that activity at the same moment neither loses their edit nor forces the routing commit to fail. Routing decisions read the authoritative work state rather than the projected read model, and work that predates the work state document adopts the projection instead of being reported as unassigned with no attempts.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterWorkStateAuthorityTests, which compiles every Contact Center source and reports each store into a routing-state field — by assignment, compound assignment, increment, decrement, or object initializer — whose receiver resolves to the CRM activity or cannot be resolved at all, self-tests that scan against the projector as a known-positive control and against the queue-item and provider-command writers as known-negative controls, and exercises a reservation concurrent with a CRM edit against a real SQLite database.

gates.gate: A live call was summarized by scalars that could not describe who was on it
gates.invariant: A call session carries the real topology of the call — legs with roles and lifecycle, a bridge whose membership history is append-only, consults, supervisor engagements, and typed relationships to other calls — and CallTopologyProjector is the only writer of any of it. Conference membership at any past instant is reconstructible from the recorded join and leave times rather than from a live count. A consultative transfer, a supervisor monitor, whisper, and barge each have a durable representation that survives the request that created them, and none of it depends on provider metadata strings.
gates.evidenceLocation: CallTopologyAuthorityTests, which scans every Contact Center source for topology mutations outside the projector, self-tests that scan against the projector as a known-positive control, pins that the scanned member names are declared exactly once so the scan cannot become ambiguous, and reconstructs conference membership at a past instant.

gates.gate: A copy of a provider voice event silently dropped the provider's hangup cause
gates.invariant: Copying a provider voice event carries every field the original declared, so a value the provider genuinely reported cannot be replaced by an inferred one without any signal that the real value was lost. Completeness is now structural rather than reviewed: the event is an immutable record, so a copy is the language's and carries every member, including any added later. What is proved instead is that the type stays that way — that it remains a record, that no property can be assigned after construction, and that no collection property is aliased from the caller, checked structurally over every property the type declares rather than by name, with a shape the check cannot build reported rather than skipped. Metadata additionally keeps the comparer it was supplied with, including when it is carried over from another event, because a snapshot that quietly became case-sensitive would change what consumers can find without changing anything they wrote.
gates.evidenceLocation: ProviderVoiceEventImmutabilityTests, which reflects over ProviderVoiceEvent to prove it is a record with no property assignable after construction, sweeps every collection property by assigning a mutable instance and growing the caller's copy to prove nothing is aliased, and exercises its metadata to prove the supplied dictionary is snapshotted with its comparer preserved through derivation.

gates.gate: A table grew forever because nobody wrote it a retention policy
gates.invariant: Every Contact Center index is either purged by a retention policy that is actually registered, or carries a written exemption naming why it is bounded without one, so a table cannot start growing unbounded through silence. Each policy ages its records from the moment they settled rather than from when they arrived or were last retried, and a table that can still hold a live record is never selected by age alone. Legal hold, the projection replay horizon, and the provider redelivery envelope only ever extend a window. The purge drains an entity across batches instead of deleting a fixed slice, spends its batch budget per entity so a later entity is never starved by an earlier one, and reports remaining work rather than completing quietly when its budget runs out. A policy may only treat statuses declared terminal by name as expired, so widening one to a status an agent still holds fails the build. Every upgrade step that adds a settlement column also backfills it, because a column added to an index does not re-project the rows that already exist and the pre-upgrade backlog would otherwise be immortal. Every settlement column an active policy ages from is stamped by a declared production statement on the transition that settles the record, so a policy cannot age from a column nothing writes; and every purge predicate is backed by a covering index leading with that column, so draining a table does not scan it end to end. No migration writes an identifier into raw SQL with a hardcoded quote, because an engine that reads that quote as a string literal turns the statement inert and skips every row without failing. The settlement stamp is required in the specific method that owns each settlement path rather than anywhere in the declaring file, so removing it from a single terminal transition fails the build. Where a second purge already targets the same table, the two windows are reconciled in both directions so neither silently overrules the other. A batch that fails partway through commits and attributes the deletes it had already staged, so partial work is never committed under a later entity's transaction and counted against nobody.
gates.evidenceLocation: ContactCenterRetentionCoverageTests, which reflects over every index and every policy to prove coverage, registration, settlement-time ageing, liveness guarding, the declared terminal-status sets, the governance floors and the settlement-column backfills; and ContactCenterRetentionPersistenceTests, which runs the real policies against a SQLite database and asserts on the survivors rather than on a deletion count, including that a tight budget starves no entity.

gates.gate: Reservation-path query-plan budget
gates.invariant: The statement routing runs before every offer — the per-agent count of live work — must be answered by seeking an index that constrains both the agent and the interaction status, on SQLite and on PostgreSQL, and must never read the interaction index table end to end. The statements measured are the ones the store executes: the hand-written statement is taken from the same builder and measured verbatim without rewriting its bound parameters, and the reservation queries the store issues through the query pipeline are captured from a recording connection, so a plan cannot be proven for a query nobody runs. The schema measured is built by the shipped migrations, so a plan cannot be proven for indexes nobody deploys. The hand-written statement must also execute successfully and return correct counts on PostgreSQL, because a plan budget cannot detect a statement that is a syntax error on the engine it targets. The declared status sets must partition InteractionStatus exactly, so a new status cannot silently drop out of "occupying an agent" and make a busy agent look idle.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/InteractionQueryPlanBudgetTests.cs asserts the SQLite plan seeks IDX_InteractionIndex_ActiveByAgent as a covering index with both AgentId and Status as seek constraints for the hand-written statement and for the pipeline-generated reservation queries captured through RecordingConnectionFactory, and that the declared status sets partition InteractionStatus; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter.DistributedTests/QueryPlans/InteractionPostgresQueryPlanBudgetTests.cs asserts the same budget on PostgreSQL via EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) and separately executes InteractionStore.CountActiveByAgentIdsAsync against a real PostgreSQL service asserting its counts, enforced by the Contact Center Operations Gates workflow's postgres service; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/AvailabilityStoreSharedDatabaseTests.cs proves the raw statement observes work written in the same uncommitted unit of work.

gates.gate: Upgrade schema convergence and startup budget
gates.invariant: A tenant that upgraded through any reachable historical schema must end up with byte-identical table and index declarations to a tenant created fresh, asserted by comparing the real declarations rather than the values the columns happen to hold: YesSql writes an enum as an integer whatever the column says, and SQLite's type affinity converts it on the way in, so a diverged column behaves correctly on SQLite forever and fails only on an engine that does not coerce. The upgrade chain is walked by return value exactly as the host walks it, so a step that no version can reach cannot be mistaken for one that runs, and every enum value an upgraded tenant already held must survive the rebuild, with an unreadable value recorded as unknown rather than rewritten to the first member. Upgrade backfills must cost the same number of database round trips regardless of how many rows the tenant holds, because they run inside the transaction that gates tenant startup and a per-row loop turns a large tenant into one that never activates.
gates.evidenceLocation: tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/Omnichannel/OmnichannelActivitySchemaConvergenceTests.cs upgrades a tenant from every reachable historical activity-index schema through MigrationChainRunner and asserts the resulting SqliteSchemaSnapshot equals a freshly created tenant's, and asserts every stored enum value round-trips after the column rebuild; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Modules/ContactCenter/MigrationStartupBudgetTests.cs runs the call-session claim backfill and the inbox canonicalization backfill against tenants that differ ten-fold in row count through RecordingConnectionFactory and asserts the statement counts are equal; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.Tests/Architecture/MigrationAdditiveOnlyGuardTests.cs authorizes the rebuild's removals only as InPlaceRebuild entries and checks the restoring operation is really present in the same migration step; tests/CrestApps.OrchardCore.ContactCenter.DistributedTests/Migrations/OmnichannelActivityPostgresMigrationTests.cs executes the upgrade against a real PostgreSQL instance from both reachable shapes of the historical schema, which is what proves the upgrade runs at all on an engine that resolves operators by type instead of merely producing the right declarations on SQLite.

gates.gate: Phone number canonicalization and fail-closed do-not-call screening
gates.invariant: A number that reaches a do-not-call registry must be the same number that will be dialed, and screening that could not be performed must never be read as screening that passed. Canonicalization happens once, through one entry point, producing a value that is in E.164 form by construction; a destination that cannot be canonicalized suppresses the attempt rather than being repaired into an approximation that no registry can compare. Within the calling and compliance path nothing may reimplement normalization or reach past that entry point to the raw parser, because a second definition of canonical form is exactly what let the dialer screen one string while the registry looked up another. A registry that cannot answer raises rather than returning an empty set, the dialer suppresses with a non-terminal reason so an unverified destination is neither dialed nor discarded, and the contact import skips the row instead of importing an unscreened number. Skill identity is subject to the same rule: a queue's requirements and an agent's assignments are read through one definition, so a skill written by a recipe matches one edited in the administration screens.

gates.gate: Every Contact Center and CRM configuration entity can leave a tenant in a deployment plan and arrive intact, under an identifier the rest of the plan still resolves
gates.invariant: A tenant that can only be configured by hand cannot be promoted. The failure this guards against is silent rather than loud: a step that hand-lists the properties it carries drops every property added after it was written, the import still succeeds, and the missing settings read as their defaults, so the loss is discovered during a cutover rather than during a build. Export and import are therefore driven by reflection over the entry type rather than by a hand-written property list, and the proof is anchored to the stored entities rather than to another export, because comparing one export against another is satisfied by a step that drops the same property on both sides. What a plan must not carry is as load-bearing as what it must: agent profiles name the person who holds them and record the state that person is in right now, so they are declared runtime state rather than configuration, and no plan carries a person between environments. Entries are exported in dependency order, since a queue that references a skill cannot be imported before it, and are reconciled by identifier and then by the members that identify them - a name, a display text, or, for entries that carry neither, the members that make one entry the same entry as another - so replaying a plan into a tenant whose migrations already seeded the same configuration updates it rather than duplicating it. Configuration is a graph and a plan is a sequence, so no ordering of the steps makes every reference resolvable at the moment it is written: a queue overflows into another queue in its own step and references a channel endpoint a different step carries. The substitutions an import makes must therefore be applied to the entries already stored as well as to the entries still to come, or the correctness of a plan depends on the order an operator happened to add its steps. Reconciling by name is only safe if each entry the destination already owned is claimed once, because nothing stops an operator from keeping two entries under one name; letting a second entry in the same plan match an entry the plan itself just created overwrites the first with the second, so two entries kept deliberately apart arrive as one and every reference to the lost entry is quietly redirected. A step that names no collection the tenant recognises imported nothing, and reporting it as executed hands the operator a tenant that looks configured because the plan ran without complaint. Reconciling by identity is not free either: the destination keeps the identifier it had already published to its own data, so every substitution has to be carried forward into the steps that follow or the plan lands with its references pointing at entries the destination does not hold - a tenant that looks configured and routes nothing, which is worse than an import that fails. A cleared setting must travel as a cleared setting rather than be omitted, or replaying a plan leaves two environments disagreeing about configuration an operator believes is synchronised. A value the owning manager derives must survive the import, or an entry means something different when it arrives in a plan than when it is created through the manager. An entry the destination rejects must be reported and skipped rather than stored, and one unusable entry must not stop the entries around it. Coverage is required of every stored entity rather than the ones someone remembered: an entity is either declared as configuration carried by a named step, or declared in writing as runtime state that must not travel between environments.

gates.gate: The public surface of every assembly another module compiles against is recorded, so changing it is a decision somebody made rather than one that happened
gates.invariant: Everything an assembly exposes publicly is a promise to whoever compiles against it, and these assemblies are compiled against by other modules in this repository and by whatever a deployment builds beside them. The surface is therefore generated from the compiled assemblies and checked in, so a change to it arrives as a diff a reviewer has to accept on purpose. Which assemblies are governed is derived from the project graph rather than listed by hand, because a list is a thing somebody has to remember to add to: a project in the Contact Center, Telephony or Omnichannel families becomes governed the moment a project that is not a packaging target compiles against it. Because a recorded surface is still only text, and text is easy to accept in bulk, the conclusions of the audit are also stated as rules: a public class is sealed unless it is abstract, introduces something overridable, or is a view model the display framework has to build a proxy from, and no public type exposes static state that anything in the process can change. Overriding an inherited member does not count as inviting derivation, and neither do the members a compiler synthesizes, or every public record would be an extension point by definition. Mutability is judged from the value a member actually holds rather than from the type it is declared as, because readonly freezes a reference and not what it points at, and a read-only interface only promises that the caller was handed no mutating method - the list behind one can be cast back and rewritten. A baseline must also be reproducible on any machine: an attribute that embeds the build directory makes the recorded surface differ on every clone and on every CI run, which leaves overwriting it the only way to pass and turns the gate into the unread bulk acceptance it exists to prevent.

gates.gate: Counting an event never makes concurrent writers meet on one row, and folding the counts afterwards neither loses a count nor counts one twice

That makes the row a serialization point for the busiest event types at the busiest hour: two handlers counting the same event on the same day either both create the row and one fails the unique constraint, or both update it under optimistic concurrency and one fails its whole request while the other overwrites a count it never read. The count is therefore appended as its own contribution, which no other writer can contend for, and a single background roller folds the contributions into the daily totals afterwards. Four things then have to hold or the totals are wrong in ways that look like nothing. The roller must delete exactly the contributions it read, because deleting by predicate would also destroy anything appended between the read and the delete and that event would be counted by nobody. It must add to the total already stored rather than replace it, because replacing passes every single-fold test while discarding every earlier fold of the same day. A reader must add the contributions not yet folded to the stored totals, or a summary read a moment after the traffic it describes reports a number behind by whatever the roller has not reached, and it must not keep counting them once folded, or it reports double. And drift detection and rebuild must account for the contributions not yet folded, or every one of them is reported as a projection that has lost counts and a real loss is indistinguishable from the roller simply not having run this minute. They must account for them without folding them: folding inside a read commits the ambient unit of work of whoever asked for the report, and folding before a rebuild reads the log makes anything recorded in between counted by the recompute and folded again on top, which inflates a business number permanently with nothing in the data to show which half is real. A rebuild is a repair that converges rather than a snapshot that is exact, and that has to be stated rather than claimed away: a contribution is written by a post-commit scope and redelivered by the outbox, so an event is in the log for a window before its contribution exists, and document identifiers are allocated before the transaction that commits them, so a contribution can become visible below a position a walk has already passed. Both leave a day high until the rebuild is run again once the projection has settled, and both must be reported by drift detection rather than being silent. The roller also has to run for every tenant that records counts, so it belongs to the feature that does the counting; registered under a feature that only some tenants enable, the totals of the rest are never folded and the contributions are purged by retention before anything reads them. The drain itself must stay bounded: the document query groups by document identity, so any ordering asked of it makes the engine sort the entire backlog before returning a single batch, which makes draining one batch cost as much as everything waiting. The rebuild's walk over the contributions not yet folded must resume from a position rather than from an offset, because the roller deletes the rows it folds from anywhere in the table: an offset would step over rows that are still waiting once earlier ones are gone, and the counts they carry would be absent from the walk, so the rebuild would write a total that is permanently short with nothing in the data to show it happened.

gates.gate: A heartbeat can neither undo a concurrent connect nor fail the agent's hub call, and the pass that signs agents out neither walks every session ever opened, nor sorts the whole backlog to return one page, nor leaves a stale agent behind a page it keeps re-reading
gates.invariant: Every connected agent sends a heartbeat on a timer, so the heartbeat is the most frequent session write the desktop performs, and the document it rewrites also carries the connection list connect and disconnect maintain. Two requirements apply at once and pull against each other: the heartbeat must not write back a connection list read before a concurrent connect committed, which the store's document-version check exists to prevent, and losing that check must not surface to the agent, whose hub call would fail on a timer over a write carrying nothing the agent needs. Neither a distributed lock nor a second read satisfies both, and the reasons are the finding worth keeping: writes are staged rather than committed, so the version check runs when the shell scope commits, which is after any lock taken inside the method has already been released, and a second read on the same unit of work is answered from that session's identity map, so it returns the instance already read rather than the row a concurrent connect committed. The stamp is therefore applied in its own unit of work, whose read reflects what is committed and which commits before returning, and a lost version check is treated as success without a retry, for a reason that differs by writer: connect and the cleanup pass carry a newer heartbeat, so a retry would write an older timestamp over a newer one, while disconnect and membership sync do not advance the heartbeat at all, so a heartbeat lost to one of those records no liveness and is tolerated because neither fires on a timer and the stale threshold spans several heartbeat intervals. On the read side, the pass that signs out agents whose heartbeats stopped runs every minute against a table holding a row for every agent who has ever connected. Three regressions there return sessions a functional test accepts and are invisible to one. Answering the cut-off by reading the table end to end costs what the deployment has accumulated rather than what actually went stale. Bounding a document query does not fix that and makes it worse: a document query groups by document identity, no ordering over the index columns can satisfy that grouping, and an ordering by document identity is supplied when a page is requested without one, so the bound introduces a sort of the entire backlog. And an unordered page leaves which sessions a pass expires to the engine, so an agent whose heartbeat stopped can sit unexpired behind a page that keeps being answered with someone else while the pass reports that it is working.

gates.gate: Creating a reservation does not read the same fact twice while holding two distributed locks, and no reservation transition depends on the lock lease for correctness
gates.invariant: The reservation locks are taken with a fixed expiration and are never renewed. A critical section that outruns its lease therefore continues believing it holds a lock it has already lost, while a second caller is admitted, and no amount of lease renewal removes that case: renewal shortens the window, it does not close it. Two properties follow. The first is that the critical section must be short, and it was not: availability is the canonical authority for whether an agent may take work, and answering that question already reads the agent profile and counts that agent's active interactions, yet the reservation path read the agent and counted its interactions a second time. Those duplicate checks were applied conjunctively, so they could only ever add a redundant rejection and never admitted an agent the authority had refused; the cost was two further round trips inside a critical section holding two unrenewed leases, and a second derivation of a decision that already had an owner. The second property is the one that actually makes an expired lease survivable, and it must be proved rather than assumed: every transition commits under a document version check, so when two callers are admitted at once, exactly one commit succeeds and the other is rejected by the database. Lease renewal is therefore not the remedy for this finding, and adding it would substitute a probabilistic defence for a deterministic one that is already in place.

gates.gate: Every event that reports an Asterisk channel has ended reaches call teardown, including when a call-control bridge absorbs the event and when a bridge throws, and no other event does
gates.invariant: Call teardown releases ARI bridges, channels, and ownership bindings, so an event that ends a channel failing to reach it leaks those resources until the reconciler sweeps. Teardown therefore runs in a finally, independently of the call-control pipeline, so it happens whether or not a bridge claimed the event and even if a bridge threw. That property was not actually gated: the test named for it dispatched a StasisStart, which is not a terminal event, so it asserted only that the dispatcher invoked teardown for some event and would have passed even if terminal teardown had been removed entirely. The bridge-absorbs case was not gated for teardown at all. Both are now gated with a real terminal event. The complementary half is that teardown must not run for anything else. A live channel emits a continuous stream of non-terminal events - state changes, DTMF, variable sets - and ends exactly once, but the dispatcher invoked every registered teardown service for every one of them and relied on each implementation to recognise a non-terminal event and refuse the work. The one shipped implementation does refuse it, on a string comparison before any store or ARI round trip, so this was a latent contract hazard rather than a live cost: the seam is an enumerable extension point whose contract told implementers they would be invoked for every event, so an implementation that read a binding before deciding would issue a store round trip per event on a per-channel event stream. The decision now lives in the dispatcher where the fan-out happens, and the terminal set now has a single named owner shared by the dispatcher and the teardown service instead of living as a private detail of one implementation. That set is deliberately narrower than the set the state mapper treats as terminal: the mapper also treats ChannelHangupRequest as terminal so it can project the call as ending, but a hangup request is a request, and destroying bridges or hanging up the peer leg on it would tear a conversation down before the channel actually ended. The two notions are kept apart on purpose.
